name: Homes of New York (HoNY) — Dobb·E Domestic Robot Learning Dataset
description: Homes of New York (HoNY) is an in-the-wild domestic robotic manipulation dataset collected across 22 real-world homes and 216 environments in New York City as part of the open-source Dobb·E robot learning framework from New York University. Recorded using 'The Stick'—a low-cost reacher-grabber tool instrumented with an iPhone LiDAR sensor—HoNY comprises 5,620 demonstration trajectories spanning 1.5 million RGB-D frames. The dataset serves as the self-supervised pretraining foundation for Home Pretrained Representations (HPR), enabling lightweight downstream robots (such as Hello Robot Stretch) to adapt to novel household tasks with as few as five minutes of target-domain demonstrations.

size.notes: HoNY RGB-D + actions archive is 77 GB (HomesOfNewYorkWithDepth.zip via Google Drive). The lightweight RGB-only release is 814 MB (homes_of_new_york.zip via dl.dobb-e.com).

provenance.collection_method: Handheld physical interaction capture using 'The Stick'—an instrumented reacher-grabber tool fitted with an iPhone recording LiDAR depth and stereo RGB, calibrated with 6-DoF gripper motion.
provenance.curation_notes: Features 216 distinct domestic environments across 22 private NYC residences. Also converted into an RLDS format for integration with Open X-Embodiment.
data_sources: Original recordings by NYU Robot Learning Lab in NYC homes
